media_work.title: After Innocence
media_work.focus_or_theme: Challenges faced by exonerees after release from wrongful imprisonment (reintegration, psychological trauma, lack of support/compensation).
media_work.summaryNotes: Won Special Jury Prize at Sundance Film Festival 2005.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Challenges faced by exonerees after release from wrongful imprisonment (reintegration, psychological trauma, lack of support/compensation).
media_item.summary_notes: This documentary focuses on the difficulties faced by individuals after exoneration. It follows seven men exonerated by DNA, exploring their emotional journeys, struggles to find work, reconnect with family, access support, and obtain compensation for the years lost to wrongful imprisonment. It contrasts the public perception of exoneration as a happy ending with the often harsh realities faced by exonerees.

research_notes_other.notes_from_film_list.txt: Follows stories of seven DNA exonerees adjusting to life after prison; Explores reintegration struggles. Directed by Jessica Sanders. Available via Amazon, DVD.
research_notes_other.research_findings: This documentary focuses on the often-overlooked difficulties faced by individuals *after* exoneration. It follows seven (list notes 7, Wikipedia lists 8) men exonerated by DNA, exploring their emotional journeys, struggles to find work, reconnect with family, access support, and obtain compensation for the years lost to wrongful imprisonment. It contrasts the public perception of exoneration as a happy ending with the often harsh realities faced by exonerees.

featured_individuals.narrative_summary: Details of Dennis Maher's case are covered elsewhere.
Wrongfully convicted of rape in Louisiana in 1982, Calvin Willis was exonerated by DNA in 2003 after serving over 21 years.
Wrongfully convicted of murder in Rhode Island in 1996, Scott Hornoff was exonerated in 2002 after the actual killer confessed, having served over 6 years.
Wrongfully convicted of rape in Florida in 1982, Wilton Dedge was exonerated by DNA in 2004 after serving 22 years.
Wrongfully convicted of rape in Pennsylvania in 1982, Vincent Moto was exonerated by DNA in 2004 after serving over 10 years.
Wrongfully convicted of kidnapping, rape, and murder in Pennsylvania in 1982 and sentenced to death, Nick Yarris was exonerated by DNA in 2004 after serving over 21 years.
Details of Ronald Cotton's case are covered elsewhere.
Wrongfully convicted of rape in California in 1988, Herman Atkins was exonerated by DNA in 2000 after serving 12 years.
